claim_reviews.conclusion: Acceptable for Indonesian school-level “student council,” though its literal scope is the intraschool student organization.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: OSIS

claim_reviews.conclusion: Valid Malaysian term for a Student Representative Council, but institutional usage is principally at universities and higher-education institutions.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: majlis perwakilan pelajar

claim_reviews.conclusion: The cue “student council” and sense “student organization representing the student body” are broadly compatible, but they underspecify educational level and institutional structure.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and stated sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Misleading as stated: the forms are not simply alternative common words for the same unrestricted concept; OSIS is school-focused, whereas MPP is chiefly university-focused. No evidence supports a false-friend relationship.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation: different-common-word

response.rationale: OSIS is an Indonesian intraschool student organization, broadly comparable to a school student council. Majlis Perwakilan Pelajar is primarily Malaysia’s university-level Student Representative Council, so the two answers are not interchangeable across the full scope of “student council.” This is an institutional-level contrast, not a false-friend contrast.
